To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) users adjust the content of their communication to the richness of a medium, 2) they adjust the time spent on different stages of the communication process to the limitations and affordances of a medium, and 3) they do not perceive the quality of the interaction to be different across media.
the communication trajectories of dyads engaged in complex problem solving tasks differ across media.
the medium moderates the message: users adapt their communication trajectories to different media in collaborative task solving.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the ways in which the use of different media influences communication processes.
the way in which people manage the complexity of their social lives and how they adapt their communication strategies to the constraints of different communication channels.
how people manage their communication in different media.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
medium moderates the message.
medium moderates the message, but not the other way around.
the media used for the task solving did not influence the decision quality, but they did affect the communication trajectories.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the medium is the message.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the effectiveness of communication does not depend on the medium, but rather on users’ ability to adjust their communicative behavior to the limitations of the medium.
ICT users employ communication strategies adapted to the particular medium they use, which results in comparable effectiveness of communication in various media.
ICT users are able to adapt their communication strategies to the limitations and affordances of different media.
